mainTopic: Finishing the impure כהן and the elderly helper's pay, then the rules on what may be bought from people suspected about בכורות, שביעית, and תרומה.
overview: This amud first finishes explaining how a כהן can become טמא while helping someone. It gives two answers: a בית הפרס, whose impurity is only rabbinic, or other impurities that a כהן is not warned against. Next, it says that an elderly helper is paid like a פועל בטל. אביי explains that this means a worker idle from his own particular job. Then a new משנה lists what we may and may not buy from someone חשוד על הבכורות. Deer meat is forbidden because it looks like calf meat. Tanned hides are allowed, and רבי אליעזר and the תנא קמא argue over female hides. The גמרא also explains the משנה's wool rules, and it says 'garments' means felt. A parallel משנה about one suspected on שביעית allows spun and woven flax, and 'woven' is explained as braided cords. Finally, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue about buying from someone suspected of selling תרומה as חולין, and a story about a suspected butcher begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A trodden-down בית הפרס is pure
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר אמי, quoting רב יהודה, rules that a בית הפרס which has been trampled into a path is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה בר אמי said in the name of רב יהודה: A בית הפרס that has been trodden down is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still explaining how the משנה can speak of a כהן becoming טמא. It brings a ruling that shows the impurity of a בית הפרס is only a rabbinic concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הפרס is a field where a grave was plowed up, so bone fragments may be scattered there. That impurity is only מדרבנן. Once people have walked over the field and trampled it into a path, we no longer worry about bones, so the area is טהור. This shows why a כהן may walk through a בית הפרס at all, even though he still should not eat תרומה before purifying himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed over, so bone fragments may be scattered there (a rabbinic impurity)
That was trodden down or trampled by people walking

steps.whyThisMatters: Because the impurity of a בית הפרס is only rabbinic, a כהן may enter one to do a service, such as examining a בכור. This is how the משנה's case of a כהן becoming impure becomes possible.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda bar Ami said in the name of Rav Yehuda:
phrases.notes: Attribution line, merged into this step.

phrases.english: A beit haperas that has been trodden down is pure.
phrases.notes: Once trampled into a path, we no longer worry about scattered bones.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer on the previous amud, which explained the משנה's impure כהן as a case of בית הפרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית הפרס that has been trodden into a path is טהור, which shows its impurity is only rabbinic.

steps.title: Another answer: other kinds of impurity
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, the משנה refers to a כהן becoming impure through other impurities, which a כהן is not forbidden to contract.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: it refers to other impurities, which priests are not warned against.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to explain the משנה's impure כהן. The case is about impurities other than contact with a dead body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids a כהן to become טמא only from a מת (a dead body). Other impurities, such as a שרץ, are not forbidden to him. However, they still stop him from eating תרומה, so he has lost something and deserves to be paid back.

keyTerms.meaning: Other kinds of impurity, not from a dead body
Warned or commanded (here: the כהנים are warned)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a כהן is forbidden to become impure in every way. The Torah's ban on a כהן covers only impurity from a dead body. Other impurities are allowed, even though they still keep him from eating תרומה.

phrases.english: Alternatively: with other impurities,
phrases.notes: A second explanation of the משנה.

phrases.english: which they (the priests) are not warned against.
phrases.notes: The ban on a כהן applies only to impurity from a dead body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation, next to the בית הפרס answer, of how a כהן can become impure in the משנה's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the משנה describes a forbidden act, since a כהן may not become impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of impurities that a כהן is allowed to contract, but that still prevent him from eating תרומה.

steps.title: An elderly helper is paid like an idle worker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about carrying an elderly helper on a donkey, and a ברייתא adds that he is paid like a פועל בטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If he was elderly, the person who needs him carries him on a donkey. It was taught in a ברייתא: he is paid like an idle worker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about an elderly examiner, judge, or witness. It brings a ברייתא that sets how much he is paid. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The examiner, judge, or witness may not take payment for the service itself. He may only be paid back for what he lost by coming. The ברייתא sets the amount: the wage of a פועל בטל, meaning someone who is kept from working.

keyTerms.meaning: He has him ride on a donkey
Like an idle worker; payment for the work he lost

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה זָקֵן — מַרְכִּיבוֹ עַל הַחֲמוֹר.
phrases.english: If he was elderly, he (the one needing him) has him ride on a donkey.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: It was taught: (he is paid) like an idle worker.
phrases.notes: A ברייתא that sets the amount of payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הָיָה זָקֵן מַרְכִּיבוֹ עַל הַחֲמוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic. It moves from the impure כהן to the elderly helper's payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The elderly helper is paid like a פועל בטל.

steps.title: אביי defines the idle worker
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that כפועל בטל means a worker idle from his own particular job.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Like a worker who is idle from that specific job of his.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains exactly what the ברייתא's phrase כפועל בטל means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The payment is not a fixed general amount. It is the sum a person in his particular trade would accept to stop his usual work and do this task instead. So both how hard his job is and how much it pays shape the amount.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often clarifies terms

steps.whatToRemember: פועל בטל = what this person would accept to leave his own job, which depends on how hard that job is and how much it pays.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line, merged into this step.

phrases.english: Like a worker idle from that specific job.
phrases.notes: The amount depends on the person's own trade.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּפוֹעֵל בָּטֵל שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא's phrase quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment is set by what this person would accept to stop his own particular work.

steps.title: New משנה: what not to buy from a suspect
steps.stepSummary: A person suspected about בכורות may not be bought from, even deer meat or untanned hides.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone suspected about firstborn animals: we may not buy deer meat from him, nor hides that are not tanned.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists products we may not buy from someone suspected of selling meat from בכורות in a forbidden way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such a person might pass off בכור meat as deer meat, which looks similar, so even deer meat is forbidden from him. Untanned hides are also forbidden, since they could come from a בכור. The words 'not tanned' suggest that tanned hides are allowed, and the גמרא will later explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
One suspected of misusing firstborn animals

steps.confusionAlert: Deer is not a בכור animal at all. It is forbidden here only because the seller might swap in בכור meat and call it deer.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of a new משנה.

phrases.english: One who is suspect regarding firstborn animals,
phrases.notes: Suspected of selling בכור meat when it is forbidden.

phrases.english: we may not buy deer meat from him,
phrases.notes: He might pass off בכור meat as deer meat.

phrases.english: nor hides that are not tanned.
phrases.notes: These could be hides of a בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From one suspected about בכורות we may not buy any meat, even deer meat, or untanned hides.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר allows hides of females
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says we may buy hides of female animals from the suspect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: We may buy hides of female animals from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר adds a lenient view. Hides of female animals may be bought from the suspect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of בכור apply only to males. A female hide can be recognized as such, so there is no worry that it came from a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who here gives a lenient view

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
phrases.notes: Attribution line, merged into this step.

phrases.english: we may buy hides of female animals from him,
phrases.notes: Only males can be בכורות.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לוֹקְחִין מִמֶּנּוּ עוֹרוֹת שֶׁל נְקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a lenient exception to the ban on untanned hides in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hides of female animals may be bought from the suspect.

steps.title: Raw wool is forbidden, but thread and garments are allowed
steps.stepSummary: We may not buy bleached or dirty wool from the suspect, but we may buy spun thread and garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we may not buy bleached or dirty wool from him, but we may buy spun thread and garments from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with rules about wool. It separates raw wool, which is forbidden, from wool that has been processed further, which is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wool of a בכור is forbidden, and raw wool, whether bleached or still dirty, could come from a בכור. Spun thread and finished garments have gone through more processing, so they are allowed. The גמרא will examine the wording of both clauses in steps 15–18.
steps.whatToRemember: From a חשוד על הבכורות, raw products (meat, untanned hides, raw wool) are forbidden. More processed products (spun thread, garments) are allowed, and female hides are allowed according to רבי אליעזר.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לוֹקְחִין מִמֶּנּוּ צֶמֶר מְלוּבָּן וְצוֹאִי,
phrases.english: And we may not buy bleached or dirty wool from him,
phrases.notes: Raw wool might be from a בכור.

phrases.english: but we may buy spun thread and garments from him.
phrases.notes: The extra processing removes the concern.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לוֹקְחִין מִמֶּנּוּ צֶמֶר מְלוּבָּן וְצוֹאִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list, moving from hides to wool.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Raw wool is forbidden from the suspect, while spun thread and garments are permitted.

steps.title: Why deer meat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the משנה forbids buying even בשר צבאים from the suspect: it can be confused with calf meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Deer meat — because it can be mistaken for calf meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. It tells us why even deer meat is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Deer are not subject to the laws of בכור at all, so you might think buying deer meat is fine. But deer meat looks like calf meat. The suspect could sell meat from a בכור calf and call it deer.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Deer meat (why is it forbidden?)
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: Because it gets confused with calf meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the rule given in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Deer meat is forbidden from the suspect because it looks like calf meat.

steps.title: Inference: tanned hides may be bought
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's words 'hides that are not tanned', the גמרא infers that tanned hides are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Nor hides that are not tanned' — this implies that tanned hides we may buy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה and draws a precise inference from its wording. The next step will explain the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only forbade untanned hides. So the גמרא reads it as permitting tanned hides. This sets up the question of why tanning should make a difference.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies (an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: Nor hides that are not tanned.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: This implies: tanned ones, we may buy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the משנה and draws an inference from its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tanned hides may be bought from the suspect.

steps.title: Why tanned hides are trusted
steps.stepSummary: A suspect would not spend effort tanning a בכור hide, because he would fear the חכמים would take it away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it really were from a בכור, he would not bother working on it. He would think: 'If the חכמים hear about it, they will make me lose it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why tanned hides are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tanning takes a lot of work and expense. A seller would not invest that much in a hide he knows is a בכור, since he risks having it taken away. So a tanned hide is almost certainly not a בכור.

phrases.english: If it were really a firstborn's hide —
he would not have bothered working on it,
(because) he thinks: if the Sages hear about it,
they will make me lose it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the inference in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tanned hide is trusted because nobody invests effort in a hide that could be taken away.

steps.title: Why does רבי אליעזר permit female hides?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's view that female hides may be bought and asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: we may buy hides of female animals from him. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר from the משנה and asks for his reason. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only males can be a בכור. Still, we need to know why we trust that the hide really comes from a female animal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
We may buy female animals' hides from him.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to רבי אליעזר's view from the משנה (Step 6) and asks for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why we trust that a hide sold as female really comes from a female.

steps.title: A female hide is recognizable
steps.stepSummary: Female hides are clearly recognizable, so the seller cannot pass off a male hide as a female one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is clearly known (whether a hide is male or female).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: you can tell from the hide itself whether the animal was male or female.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The skin shows the animal's body differences. Because of this, a seller cannot fake a female hide, so there is no fear of a בכור.

phrases.english: It is clearly recognizable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sex of the animal is visible from the hide.

steps.title: The תנא קמא fears the 'mice' excuse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא forbids female hides. The answer: the seller could cut off the male part and claim mice ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא (why does he forbid)? If so, with a male hide too, he will cut off the male organ and say 'mice ate it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא disagrees, and answers in the same breath. He is worried about a trick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא agrees that a female hide can be recognized. But he worries that a seller will cut away the male part of a בכור hide. Then he will explain the missing piece by saying mice chewed it.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (anonymous) תנא in the משנה

phrases.english: And the first Tanna (why does he forbid)?
phrases.notes: A short, implied question.

phrases.english: If so, a male (hide) also —
he will cut off its male organ
and say, 'Mice ate it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the opposing view, which is not satisfied by the reason in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seller could remove the male part and blame mice.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: mouse damage is recognizable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר is not worried, because you can tell a mouse bite apart from a knife cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other (רבי אליעזר)? The place of mice is clearly recognizable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אליעזר rejects the תנא קמא's worry. Mouse damage looks different from a deliberate cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mouse bites leave a ragged, gnawed edge. A knife leaves a clean cut. So the seller's 'mice ate it' excuse would be exposed, and רבי אליעזר keeps his ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole מחלוקת depends on whether a fake ('mice ate it') can be detected. Tanned hides are allowed because no one would invest effort in a בכור hide. Deer meat is forbidden because it can pass for calf meat.

phrases.english: And the other (Rabbi Eliezer)?
A place eaten by mice is clearly recognizable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אליעזר's reply to the תנא קמא's concern in Step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר holds that cutting and blaming mice would be detected, so female hides may be bought.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר is not worried about the 'mice ate it' excuse, because mouse damage can be told apart from a deliberate cut.

steps.title: Why mention dirty wool if bleached wool is already forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on buying bleached or dirty wool and asks why dirty wool needs to be listed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says we may not buy bleached or dirty wool from him. But if we may not even buy bleached wool, is it necessary to say dirty wool?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line of the משנה and points out that one of its two cases seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bleached wool has had work put into it, so you might think the seller would not bother doing that work on בכור wool. If even bleached wool is forbidden, then dirty wool, with no work done at all, is obviously forbidden. So why does the משנה list dirty wool?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now that... is it necessary?' The question used when one case already makes another obvious

phrases.english: And one may not buy from him
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה about the one suspected regarding בכור

phrases.english: bleached wool and dirty wool.
Now, if bleached wool we do not buy,
phrases.notes: Even though work was invested in it

phrases.english: is it necessary to say dirty wool?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא צֶמֶר מְלוּבָּן לָא זָבְנִינַן, צוֹאִי מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the hides discussion to the next clause of the משנה, about wool.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה listing both bleached and dirty wool
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the harder case (bleached) is forbidden, the easier case (dirty) does not need to be said.

steps.title: It is one case: wool cleaned of its dirt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is describing a single case: wool that was only cleaned of its dirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is teaching one case: wool that was whitened by removing its dirt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the two words as one description instead of two separate cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Bleached and dirty' really means wool made white just by washing out its dirt. That is only a small amount of work, so it does not prove the seller would avoid doing it to בכור wool. That is why it is still forbidden, and nothing in the משנה is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It teaches one thing.' The two terms describe a single case

phrases.english: Rather, it is teaching one case:
wool whitened from its dirt.
phrases.notes: Simply washed clean, with little effort invested

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording: two words become one case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bleached and dirty are two separate cases, so dirty seems extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one case: wool only washed of its dirt, which takes too little work to prove anything.
steps.whatToRemember: Washing wool is too little work to show it is not בכור, so you still may not buy it.

steps.title: Why mention garments if spun thread is already allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows spun thread and garments. The גמרא asks why garments need to be listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one may buy spun thread and garments from him. If we may buy spun thread, is it necessary to say garments?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה and asks the same kind of question in reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spinning takes a lot of work, so the seller would not risk doing it on בכור wool that the חכמים could take away. That is why spun thread is allowed. Garments need even more work, so allowing them seems obvious.

phrases.english: But one may buy from him
spun thread and garments.
Now, if spun thread we buy,
is it necessary to say garments?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'isn't it obvious?' pattern on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word בגדים in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If spun thread (less work) is allowed, garments (more work) are obviously allowed.

steps.title: Garments means felt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'garments' here means felt, which is not made from spun thread.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'garments' mean? Felt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by explaining which kind of garments the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Felt is made by pressing wool together, not by spinning it. So the reason given for spun thread does not cover felt, and the משנה needs to say directly that felt is also allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: What? Used to ask for the meaning of a word

phrases.english: What is meant by 'garments'?
Felt.
phrases.notes: Made without spinning

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the term as a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Garments' means ordinary woven clothing made from spun thread.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Garments' means felt, which is made without spinning, so it needed its own mention.

steps.title: New משנה: buying flax from one suspected about שביעית
steps.stepSummary: From someone suspected about שביעית you may not buy flax, even combed flax, but you may buy spun thread and woven cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone suspected about שביעית: we do not buy flax from him, not even combed flax. But we may buy spun thread and woven cloth from such people.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה applies the same kind of rules to someone suspected of breaking the laws of שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw flax, and even combed flax that took work, might be forbidden שביעית produce, so we do not buy it. Once it has been spun or woven, we are allowed to buy it from him, just like spun wool in the בכור case.

keyTerms.meaning: One suspected of breaking the laws of שביעית

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who is suspected about the Sabbatical Year:
one may not buy flax from him,
and even combed flax,
phrases.notes: Even though work went into it

phrases.english: but one may buy from them spun thread and woven cloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה with a parallel rule, now about שביעית instead of בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flax, even combed, may not be bought from one suspected about שביעית. Spun thread and woven cloth may be bought.
steps.confusionAlert: Combed flax (סרק) is still forbidden even though work went into it. Only spinning or weaving makes it allowed.

steps.title: Why mention woven cloth if spun thread is allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to list woven cloth once it has allowed spun thread.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: If we may buy spun thread, is it necessary to say woven cloth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same pattern as before, now on the new משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Woven cloth is made from spun thread and takes even more work. If spun thread is allowed, woven cloth seems obviously allowed too, so the word אריג looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Now, if spun thread we buy,
is it necessary to say woven cloth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the question pattern of step 17, now about the שביעית משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word אריג in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Woven cloth needs more work than spun thread, so allowing it should go without saying.

steps.title: Woven means braided cords
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'woven' means braided cords, which are not made from spun thread.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'woven' mean? Braided cords.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers, just as with felt, by explaining what kind of item the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיכי are braided or plaited cords made without spinning. Since they are not spun, the rule for spun thread would not cover them, so the משנה had to say they are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Braided cords or chains, not made from spun thread

phrases.english: What is meant by 'woven'?
Braided cords.
phrases.notes: Made without spinning

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the term as a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Woven' means ordinary cloth woven from spun thread.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Woven' means braided cords made without spinning, so it needed its own mention.
steps.whatToRemember: Pattern of this section: when a later item seems obvious, the גמרא explains it as an item made without spinning (felt, braided cords), which needed its own ruling.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: buy nothing at all from someone suspected about תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that if someone is suspected of selling תרומה as if it were חולין, you may not buy even water and salt from him. This is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a person is suspected of selling תרומה as ordinary food, you may not buy even water and salt from him. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a seller who is suspected of selling holy תרומה while claiming it is ordinary food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water and salt never become תרומה, so this ruling is very strict. רבי יהודה treats this seller as so untrustworthy that you should not buy anything at all from him.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. The marker מַתְנִי׳ shows that a new משנה is starting.
The portion of produce given to a כהן. It is holy and forbidden to non-כהנים.
Under the name of ordinary, non-holy food. In other words, passing it off as regular produce.
A person who is suspected of doing something wrong.

steps.confusionAlert: Water and salt can never be תרומה. רבי יהודה is not saying they could be תרומה. He is saying that this seller should not be bought from at all.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of a new משנה.

phrases.english: One who is suspected of selling
terumah as if it were ordinary produce
one may not buy from him
even water and salt;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הֶחָשׁוּד לִהְיוֹת מוֹכֵר תְּרוּמָה לְשׁוּם חוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from people suspected about שביעית to a new kind of suspect: someone suspected of passing off תרומה as חולין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, nothing may be bought from a person suspected of selling תרומה as חולין, not even water and salt.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: only items that תרומה can apply to are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי יהודה. He forbids buying only items that have a connection to תרומה and מעשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Anything that has a connection to תרומה and מעשרות may not be bought from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a narrower rule than רבי יהודה. You only need to avoid items that could actually involve תרומה or מעשרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי שמעון, water and salt are allowed, because תרומה and מעשרות never apply to them. The worry is limited to things where real תרומה could be hidden. His general wording, 'anything that has a connection,' sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A connection or link. Here it means that the item could be affected by תרומה.
Tithes, the required portions separated from produce.
Anything that has in it. This broad wording is what the גמרא will examine.

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא will ask what this broad phrase includes beyond the obvious cases.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ זִיקַּת תְּרוּמָה וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת
phrases.english: anything that has a connection to terumah and tithes
one may not buy from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ זִיקַּת תְּרוּמָה וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting, more lenient view to רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, only items that תרומה and מעשרות can apply to may not be bought from the suspect. Water and salt are allowed.

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון's broad wording add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case רבי שמעון's general phrase is meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי שמעון's words. It is setting up the next step, where the answer will come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון could have simply said 'produce.' Instead he said 'anything that has a connection,' which sounds broader. The גמרא wants to know which non-obvious item this wording adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה. The marker גְּמָ׳ shows it is starting.
To include what? The גמרא uses this to ask what an extra or broad phrase adds.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What does this come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the broad wording of רבי שמעון's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra item is included by the phrase 'anything that has a connection to תרומה and מעשרות'?

steps.title: It includes fish innards, since olive oil is mixed into them
steps.stepSummary: The broad wording includes fish innards. People mix olive oil into them, and that oil could be תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include fish innards, because people mix olive oil into them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. רבי שמעון's wording is meant to forbid fish innards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish are not produce, so you would think תרומה has nothing to do with them. But fish innards are usually prepared with olive oil, and olive oil can be תרומה. That is why they count as having a 'connection' to תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Olive oil, which can be תרומה.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, the test is whether a תרומה ingredient could be mixed in. Even fish innards are forbidden from this seller because of the olive oil in them.

phrases.english: To include fish innards,
since people mix olive oil into them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what רבי שמעון's broad wording adds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase includes fish innards, because they contain olive oil that could be תרומה.

steps.title: A story begins about a suspected butcher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts telling a story about a butcher who was suspected of selling something improperly. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain butcher who was suspected of selling...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about a real case. This line only sets up the story, and the details come in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After teaching the rules about suspected sellers, the גמרא brings a real-life case of a butcher under suspicion. What he was suspected of selling, and how it was handled, will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain (person). This word often opens a story in the גמרא.

phrases.english: There was a certain butcher
who was suspected of selling
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rules about suspected sellers to a real case involving a suspected butcher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This line only opens the story. No ruling has been stated yet.
